summary: Consolidated finding submitted for fresh execution with the missing bounded-progress element. The successor harness keeps the same scenario (three Node-API nodes, committed remove-3 then add-3, stable leader 1) and adds two retry attempts on the re-added voter (900 ms contexts, 800 ms windows) interleaved with proposals by never-removed node 2 that the cluster commits in the same intervals, plus the existing control and post-leader-change repair cases. Four comparisons were added (retry1_result, retry2_result, progress1_commit, progress2_commit) so repeated nonprogress and concurrent cluster progress are evaluated separately; a local dry run in the scratch copy shows all eleven comparisons complete and satisfied (both retries returned false with leader 1 stable and voter true, both paired member proposals committed on all three nodes). Rationale: a bounded progress account needs repeated nonprogress under fair opportunities with no enabled repair, which the single-invocation predecessor did not establish.
